title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
hints: this looks like edit distance or delete-operation-for-two-strings, but instead of counting deletions, each deletion now has a cost equal to its character's ASCII value
define dp[i][j] as the minimum total ASCII cost of deletions needed to make the first i characters of s1 and the first j characters of s2 equal
if s1[i-1] == s2[j-1], that character can stay in both for free: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]
if they differ, you must delete one of them (whichever is cheaper): dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j] + ascii(s1[i-1]), dp[i][j-1] + ascii(s2[j-1]))
base cases: dp[i][0] is the cost of deleting all of s1's first i characters (running ASCII sum), and dp[0][j] is the same for s2; fill the table and return dp[m][n]
commonMistakes: counting deletions (adding 1) instead of adding the actual ASCII value of the deleted character
forgetting the base case rows/columns need running ASCII sums, not just running counts
picking the wrong branch to delete from when characters differ, instead of comparing both costs and taking the minimum

content.problemStatement:
You're given two strings `s1` and `s2`.

**Find the lowest possible sum of ASCII values of the characters you must delete (from either string) so that the two strings become identical.**

Unlike simply counting deletions, here every deleted character costs its
ASCII value, so deleting an 'a' (97) is cheaper than deleting a 'z' (122).
constraints: strings consist of lowercase English letters
notes: the two strings are already identical (cost is 0)
the two strings share no characters at all (delete every character from both)
one string is empty (delete every character of the other)

sampleTestCases.explanation: Deleting 's' (115) from "sea" and both 't' (116) from "eat" leaves "ea" in common... actually deleting 's' from s1 and 't' from s2 leaves "ea" in both, costing 115 + 116 = 231.
Deleting "dee" from "delete" (100+101+101=302) and "e" from "leet" (101) leaves "let" common to both, for a total cost of 403.

optimal.space: O(m * n), reducible to O(min(m, n))
optimal.pattern: 2D dynamic programming over two string indices, minimizing ASCII cost instead of counting

bruteForce.approach: recursively try, at each position, deleting the current character from s1, deleting from s2, or keeping both if they match, summing ASCII costs and taking the minimum over all branches
